lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Application or project: helper tools and adult-only tools

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice helper tools and adult-only tools. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: A trusted adult lays out five or six real kitchen tools on a clean counter, including at least one clearly adult-only tool.
safetyNotes: A trusted adult stays in the room and handles every adult-only tool named during this task.
The learner never picks up or handles a knife with a sharp blade, the stove, the oven, or any small appliance during this lesson.
If the learner is unsure which group a tool belongs in, the correct move is to ask the adult before touching it, and that asking counts as success.

simulationAlternative.description: If real kitchen tools are not available to lay out, the learner instead sorts six printed or hand-drawn pictures of kitchen tools into the two groups and, for each one, writes the specific reason it belongs there (sharp edge, heat, or electrical part versus none of those).

materials: adult-or-local: five or six real kitchen tools, including at least one adult-only tool

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Was there a tool you thought belonged in one group but your adult said it belonged in the other? Describe the tool and what you learned about it.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Sorting accuracy: Sorts all tools correctly, with adult confirmation, into helper or adult-only. | Reasoning: Gives a reason grounded in sharpness, heat, or electricity for most tools. | Boundary respected: Points to or names adult-only tools without touching them. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner sort three additional tools from a different room, such as the bathroom or garage, into helper and adult-only groups using the same three reasons, showing the rule transfers beyond the kitchen.

duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

resources.title: helper tools and adult-only tools worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: A trusted adult lays out five or six real kitchen tools on a clean counter, including at least one clearly adult-only tool.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact helper tools and adult-only tools decision or action.
Model move 2: Before sorting, look at all the tools your adult has laid out.
Model move 3: With your adult watching, pick up or point to each tool one at a time, say which group it belongs in out loud, and explain your reason before moving to the next tool.

Model check: Sorting accuracy: Sorts all tools correctly, with adult confirmation, into helper or adult-only. | Reasoning: Gives a reason grounded in sharpness, heat, or electricity for most tools. | Boundary respected: Points to or names adult-only tools without touching them.

resources.title: helper tools and adult-only tools action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for helper tools and adult-only tools.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: helper tools and adult-only tools coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: A trusted adult lays out five or six real kitchen tools on a clean counter, including at least one clearly adult-only tool.
Coach direction: Before sorting, look at all the tools your adult has laid out.
Learner prompt: List the tools you see on the counter, one per line.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: helper tools and adult-only tools complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your adult watching, pick up or point to each tool one at a time, say which group it belongs in out loud, and explain your reason before moving to the next tool.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I named a group (helper tool or adult-only tool) for every tool on the counter.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I gave a reason based on sharpness, heat, or electricity, not a guess.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I did not pick up any adult-only tool myself.

Equal-access rule: If real kitchen tools are not available to lay out, the learner instead sorts six printed or hand-drawn pictures of kitchen tools into the two groups and, for each one, writes the specific reason it belongs there (sharp edge, heat, or electrical part versus none of those).

resources.title: helper tools and adult-only tools minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Was there a tool you thought belonged in one group but your adult said it belonged in the other? Describe the tool and what you learned about it.

Success checks: Sorting accuracy: Sorts all tools correctly, with adult confirmation, into helper or adult-only. | Reasoning: Gives a reason grounded in sharpness, heat, or electricity for most tools. | Boundary respected: Points to or names adult-only tools without touching them.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: helper tools and adult-only tools supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional helper tools and adult-only tools condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Sorting accuracy: Sorts all tools correctly, with adult confirmation, into helper or adult-only. | Reasoning: Gives a reason grounded in sharpness, heat, or electricity for most tools. | Boundary respected: Points to or names adult-only tools without touching them..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Sorting accuracy: Sorts all tools correctly, with adult confirmation, into helper or adult-only. | Reasoning: Gives a reason grounded in sharpness, heat, or electricity for most tools. | Boundary respected: Points to or names adult-only tools without touching them.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u03-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
